title: Even out a cabinet flap door's gaps with the hinge's side screw, then close it
instruction: Even out the gaps either side of the open cabinet flap door with the red screwdriver, then close the door and let go.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00) and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00), over 2 million US workers together, re-centre cabinet doors on cup hinges after installation and whenever a door starts to rub. They turn the side-adjust screw on the hinge arm, close the door to check the reveals, and leave the depth and clamp screws alone, because loosening the clamp lets the arm slip and the door sag.
setup: Station table; metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; heights below are above the table top (z 0.7475). (1) Cabinet run (fixed, 30 kg, 18 mm oak-veneer chipboard, sRGB (0.80, 0.74, 0.60)): a plinth block 300 x 470 x 96 mm at x 0.20 to 0.50, y -0.235 to 0.235; bottom board 300 x 470 x 18 at z 0.100 to 0.118; dividers at y -0.162 and 0.162, outer walls at y -0.244 and 0.244 (300 x 18 x 288, z 0.100 to 0.388); back board at x 0.482 to 0.500; a 60 x 470 x 18 back stretcher at x 0.41 to 0.47, z 0.370 to 0.388; no top board (open-topped base unit, worktop not yet fitted). (2) Two neighbouring flap doors (fixed, 18 x 82 x 270 mm, grey laminate sRGB (0.62, 0.64, 0.68)) at x 0.182 to 0.200, z 0.100 to 0.370, y 0.153 to 0.235 and -0.235 to -0.153; they are the left and right neighbours of the middle flap and continue beyond the modelled strip. (3) Flap door (the middle unit's): 297 (y) x 18 (x) x 270 (z) mm MDF with grey laminate, same colour, 1.05 kg with its 35 x 35 x 12 mm steel hinge-cup boss; hinged along its bottom outer edge, axis along y at x 0.182, z 0.100; closed it fills x 0.182 to 0.200, y -0.1485 to 0.1485 (4.5 mm reveal each side), z 0.100 to 0.370. A lift stay (0.7 N m/rad) takes most of its weight; a self-closing catch (3.0 N m/rad, damped) pulls it shut over the last 50 deg; the hinge friction is 0.1 N m. It starts open 90 deg, lying flat at z 0.100 to 0.118 in front of the unit, flush with the bottom board. (4) Hinge arm (steel, sRGB (0.55, 0.57, 0.60), 50 g, 64 x 39 x 10 mm) at (0.220, 0.070, 0.110) carries the door on a slide that moves it sideways, in and out and down; a mounting tab 40 x 60 x 6 mm at x 0.212 to 0.252, y 0.040 to 0.100, z 0.118 to 0.124 carries three slotted cam heads (zinc, 7 x 7.8 x 5 mm, 5 g, slot 1.8 mm wide and 3 mm deep, widening over a 2 mm chamfer to 3.8 mm at the top, z 0.124 to 0.129) at y 0.070: clamp screw at x 0.220, side cam at x 0.232, depth cam at x 0.244. Nothing marks which is which. Each head turns against 0.004 N m of friction (check with a 0.1 to 1 N cm torque screwdriver). The clamp screw starts tight (it only loosens, counter-clockwise from above); loosened more than 25 deg it lets the arm slip 2.5 mm down for good. The side cam is an eccentric of 3.0 mm throw (door moves 3.0 mm x sin of its angle, stops at +-90 deg); it starts 39.3 deg off neutral, so the door sits 1.9 mm toward its left neighbour: reveals 6.4 mm on the right and 2.6 mm on the left. The depth cam is an eccentric of 2.0 mm throw (door proud by 2.0 mm x sin of its angle), starting at neutral. (5) Screwdriver: stubby slotted driver, 75 mm overall, 140 g, red PP handle 22 mm diameter and 45 mm long, steel shaft 5 mm diameter and 22 mm long, blade 5.0 x 0.9 x 8 mm, friction 0.8 / 0.7; it stands blade-down in the rack with the handle's shoulder on the plate, blade tip at (0.070, 0.210, 0.0125). (6) Holder rack (fixed, 1.0 kg, steel grey): a 80 x 80 x 6 mm plate at z 0.0365 to 0.0425 with a 16 mm square hole, on four 8 x 8 mm legs at (+-0.036, +-0.036) from (0.070, 0.210).
scoring: Measured every control step from reset with the door's hinge line (a linkkit History updated each step and cleared only by the simulator reset): psi = door opening angle, gR / gL = reveal to the right / left neighbour (mm, from the door's lateral position), proud = door face forward of flush (mm), sag = hinge line below nominal (mm), th = side-cam angle. Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: sag of 1.2 mm or more (the clamp screw was loosened, the arm slipped; retightening cannot undo it). Closed = psi at most 3 deg. Even = closed with |gR - gL| at most 1.0 mm and each reveal 3.0 to 6.0 mm. Flush = |proud| at most 0.6 mm. Ladder: 0.25 = at the end the side cam is at least 10 deg nearer neutral than it started (|th| at most 29.3 deg); 0.5 = the door was closed with even reveals at some time, but not at the end; 0.75 = at the end closed, even, flush and the door still (under 3 mm/s) for 1 s; 1.0 = also the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the door and the driver, both grippers under 5 mm/s for 1 s, and the driver tip out of every slot. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Whole-run history is cleared only by the simulator reset, so loosening the clamp and tightening it again never clears the gate. Real trial: feeler gauges (3.0 and 6.0 mm go/no-go, and a 1.0 mm difference check) for the reveals on the closed door at mid height; a steel straightedge across the neighbouring faces and a 0.6 mm feeler for flush; a dial indicator or ruler on the door's bottom edge for sag (1.2 mm); a protractor or angle finder on the door and scribe marks with a protractor on the side cam head for its angle; video for the door being still and for pads 30 mm clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the door 90 deg onto its stop. Turn the side cam to 39.3 deg counter-clockwise from neutral (a scribed mark), the depth cam to neutral, and tighten the clamp screw to its stop. Check the reveals with feeler gauges (6.4 mm right, 2.6 mm left, flush, no sag). Stand the screwdriver blade-down in the rack. The cabinet and the rack are fixed on taped outlines.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The cup hinge's four-bar linkage is one pivot on a three-axis slide; cam angles drive the slide in software (eccentric law, 0.004 N m head friction), the clamp slip is a latched 2.5 mm drop, and the lift stay and soft-close are joint springs. The run is cut to a 470 mm strip with 82 mm neighbour flaps, open-topped (no top board) so the arm can reach in; hinge arm 64 mm long. Blade-in-slot torque is real contact.
